q: Which state of matter can be compressed easily?
explain: Gas particles are far apart with a lot of empty space between them, so they can be pushed closer together. Particles in solids and liquids are already touching.

q: The air pressure in a car tyre rises after a long journey. Which is the correct explanation?
options: The air particles gain kinetic energy, so they hit the walls of the tyre more often and with greater force.
Friction creates more air particles inside the tyre.
The air particles stick to the inside wall of the tyre.
explain: A warmer gas has faster particles, and at constant volume this raises the pressure.

q: Which change of state is the reverse of condensing?
explain: Condensing is gas to liquid, so the reverse is liquid to gas, which is evaporating (or boiling).

q:
Four substances have these melting points and boiling points.
W: −95 °C and 69 °C
X: 98 °C and 883 °C
Y: −182 °C and −162 °C
Z: 1085 °C and 2562 °C
Which substance is a liquid at 25 °C?
explain: W has a melting point below 25 °C and a boiling point above 25 °C. X and Z are solids and Y is a gas at 25 °C.

q: The pressure of a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature is increased from 1 atm to 3 atm. Which statement about the volume of the gas is correct?
options: It becomes three times the original volume.
It becomes the same as the original volume.
It becomes one third of the original volume.
It becomes half of the original volume.
explain: At constant temperature, volume is inversely proportional to pressure, so tripling the pressure reduces the volume to one third.

q: Oxygen melts at −218 °C and boils at −183 °C. In which state is oxygen at −200 °C?
options: A mixture of liquid and gas
explain: −200 °C is higher than the melting point (−218 °C) but lower than the boiling point (−183 °C), so oxygen is a liquid.

q: Two gases are at the same temperature and have the same average kinetic energy. Why does the lighter gas diffuse faster?
options: Lighter particles have more kinetic energy.
For the same kinetic energy, lighter particles must move at a higher speed.
Lighter particles are attracted less to the container walls.
Lighter particles do not collide with other particles.
explain: Kinetic energy depends on both mass and speed, so a particle with less mass needs a greater speed to have the same kinetic energy.

q: Which statement correctly distinguishes boiling from evaporating?
options: Boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point, but evaporating happens only at the surface and at any temperature.
Boiling happens only at the surface, but evaporating happens throughout the liquid.
Boiling happens at any temperature, but evaporating happens only at the boiling point.
Boiling happens only below the boiling point, but evaporating happens only above it.
explain: Bubbles of vapour form inside the liquid during boiling at the boiling point, whereas evaporation is a surface process that occurs at all temperatures.

q: The same mass of a substance is in each of its three states. In which state does it occupy the largest volume?
options: The volume is the same in all three states
explain: The particles in a gas are far apart, so the gas takes up much more space than the same number of particles in a solid or liquid.

q: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 120 cm³ at a pressure of 100 kPa. The pressure is doubled at constant temperature. What is the new volume of the gas?
explain: At constant temperature, volume is inversely proportional to pressure, so doubling the pressure halves the volume: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 cm³.

q: Which statement about a gas is correct?
options: It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume.
It has a fixed volume and cannot be compressed.
It keeps the same volume when moved to a larger container.
It has no fixed shape and fills the container it is in.
explain: Gas particles move freely in all directions, so the gas spreads out to fill any container.

q: A drop of food colouring is added to a beaker of hot water and to a beaker of cold water. Which observation is correct?
options: The colour spreads faster in the cold water.
The colour spreads faster in the hot water because the particles have more energy and move faster.
The colour spreads at the same rate in both.
The colour spreads faster in the hot water because the dye particles become smaller.
explain: A higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so diffusion is faster.

q: A gas jar of brown bromine vapour is placed under a gas jar of air with a lid between them. The lid is removed and the brown colour spreads upwards into the top jar, even though bromine is denser than air. What does this show?
options: Bromine reacts with air to form a brown gas.
Bromine is less dense than air.
The particles move randomly and spread out by diffusion.
explain: The brown colour moves upwards against gravity because the particles move randomly, which is diffusion.

q:
The temperature of a pure substance is recorded as it is heated at a steady rate.
0–2 minutes: rises from −20 °C to 0 °C
2–6 minutes: stays at 0 °C
6–14 minutes: rises from 0 °C to 100 °C
14–26 minutes: stays at 100 °C
What is present after 20 minutes?
explain: The temperature is constant at 100 °C between 14 and 26 minutes, which is the boiling point, so liquid and gas are both present.

q: A tyre pump is used with its outlet blocked. The air inside is compressed to a smaller volume at constant temperature. What happens to the spaces between the air particles?
explain: Compression pushes the gas particles closer together, but they never completely touch while it is still a gas.

q: A sealed rigid flask of gas is placed in boiling water. Which row shows what happens to the gas?
explain: The flask is sealed, so the number of particles is unchanged. Heating makes the particles faster, so they hit the walls harder and more often and the pressure rises.

q: Which gas diffuses most slowly at the same temperature and pressure?
explain: Cl₂ has the largest Mr (71, compared with 64, 44 and 28), so it diffuses slowest.

q: Why does a puddle dry faster on a hot day than on a cool day?
options: The water boils on the surface of the puddle.
A greater proportion of the surface particles have enough energy to escape.
The air particles push the water particles out.
explain: At a higher temperature more water particles have enough energy to escape from the surface, so the rate of evaporation is higher.

q: Which statement about the change from liquid to gas is correct?
options: The covalent bonds inside the molecules break.
The energy overcomes the forces between particles, so they move far apart and move independently.
explain: Boiling separates whole particles from one another. The bonds within each molecule stay intact.

q: The smell of perfume takes several seconds to reach the other side of a still room, even though perfume particles move very fast. Why?
options: The perfume particles move very slowly.
The perfume particles keep colliding with air particles and changing direction.
The air particles push the perfume particles back to the start.
The perfume particles need to be heated first.
explain: Frequent collisions with air particles make the path of each particle a zigzag, so the net spread is slow.

q: Which change makes the smell of a gas spread faster through a room?
options: Decreasing the temperature of the room
Increasing the temperature of the room
Putting the gas in a larger container
explain: Warmer particles move faster, so diffusion is faster.

q: Which noble gas diffuses most slowly at the same temperature and pressure?
explain: Krypton has the largest relative atomic mass, so its atoms move the most slowly at a given temperature.

q: Chlorine melts at −101 °C and boils at −35 °C. In which state is chlorine at −50 °C?
options: A mixture of solid and gas
explain: −50 °C is above the melting point (−101 °C) and below the boiling point (−35 °C), so chlorine is a liquid.

q: Ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas meet inside a glass tube and form a white ring. Which equation represents the reaction?
explain: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride react in a 1 : 1 ratio to form the white solid ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl.

q: Which row correctly describes diffusion?
options: Liquid | Vibrate in fixed positions | Slow
Solid | Move freely and randomly | Fast
Gas | Slide past one another | Slow
Gas | Move freely and randomly | Fast
explain: Gas particles move freely and randomly, so diffusion is fast. Liquid particles slide past each other, and solid particles only vibrate.

q: Drops of water form on a cold window when warm, damp air touches it. Which change of state is this?
explain: Water vapour in the air is cooled by the window and changes from gas to liquid, which is condensing.

q:
The time taken for 100 cm³ of each gas to diffuse through a porous pot is measured at the same temperature.
Gas R: 20 s
Gas S: 35 s
Gas T: 50 s
Which gas has the greatest relative molecular mass?
options: They have the same relative molecular mass
explain: The gas with the longest diffusion time diffuses slowest, so it has the greatest relative molecular mass.

q: Which row correctly describes the particles in the state shown?
options: Liquid | Regular pattern | Slide past one another
Gas | Random | Vibrate about fixed positions
Solid | Random | Vibrate about fixed positions
Solid | Regular pattern | Vibrate about fixed positions
explain: A solid has a regular pattern and its particles vibrate about fixed positions. Liquids are random and slide past each other, while gases are random and move freely.

q: Which statement is the best description of diffusion?
options: The movement of particles from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration.
The movement of particles caused only by stirring.
The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, caused by their random motion.
The breaking up of particles into smaller particles.
explain: Particles move randomly, and overall more move from the area where they are more concentrated into the area where they are less concentrated.

q: Which row correctly describes a change of state of a pure substance?
explain: Melting and boiling absorb energy, condensing and freezing release energy, and the temperature of a pure substance stays constant during each change of state.
